# `scss/max-nesting-depth`

**Limit nesting depth**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Pack** | `@codelaw/rules-scss` (npm) · `codelaw-rules-scss` (PyPI) |
| **Languages** | SCSS |
| **Turned on by** | `codelaw:scss/strict` at `error` |
| **Severity when named without one** | `error` |
| **Options** | `max` |
| **Fix** | `manual` — no automatic fix; the steps are under *How to fix* (flattening a selector is the author's call) |
| **Stability** | `preview` — runs only with `preview = true` |
| **Since** | 0.3.0 |
| **Ported from** | `stylelint/max-nesting-depth` |

## What it checks

A style rule nests at most `max` levels inside other style rules (default 3): `.a { .b { .c { .d {} } } }` is three levels of nesting.

**Why:** Deep nesting couples a rule to the markup's shape, raises specificity, and produces long selectors nobody wrote on purpose.

## Configuration

Everything below goes in `codelaw.toml` at the repo root. The same keys work as `[tool.codelaw]` in `pyproject.toml` or `"codelaw"` in `package.json` ([SR-CONFIG](../../../records/0110_config.md)).

### Turn it on

**Install the pack** (`codelaw init` does it for the languages it finds):

```bash
npm install --save-dev @codelaw/rules-scss
pip install codelaw-rules-scss
```

**Then extend a preset that turns it on** — `codelaw:scss/strict` sets it to `error`:

```toml
preview = true                        # pack rules are preview today
extends = ["codelaw:scss/strict"]
```

- **A rule exists only once its pack is loaded** through `extends`; naming it in `[rules]` without that is an unknown rule id (exit 2).
- **Without `preview = true`** the rule is skipped and codelaw warns that it is preview.

### Severity

```toml
[rules]
"scss/max-nesting-depth" = "warn"    # error | warn | info | off
```

- **`error`** fails the run (exit 1) · **`warn`** fails only with `--max-warnings N` · **`info`** never fails · **`off`** turns it off.
- **Naming it with a severity turns it on** even when no preset does.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `max` | `number` | `3` | the deepest nesting allowed |

**Every option at its default** — a starting point to copy:

```toml
[rules."scss/max-nesting-depth"]
severity = "error"

[rules."scss/max-nesting-depth".options]
max = 3
```

**The same, inline, with example values:**

```toml
[rules]
"scss/max-nesting-depth" = { severity = "error", options = { max = 6 } }
```

- **A table without `severity`** changes only the options: the severity stays what a preset or an earlier layer set, and a rule that is off stays off.
- **A list option replaces its default** — copy the default entries you want to keep.
- **An unknown option or a value of the wrong type** stops the run with exit 2 and names the nearest option.

#### `max`

*number* · default `3`

the deepest nesting allowed

```toml
[rules."scss/max-nesting-depth".options]
max = 6
```

### For a group of files

A `[scope.<name>]` gives some files their own setting, applied after `[rules]` — a scope of your own needs `files`:

```toml
[scope.legacy]
files = ["src/legacy/**/*.scss"]
rules = { "scss/max-nesting-depth" = { options = { max = 6 } } }
```

Or switch it off there:

```toml
[scope.legacy]
files = ["src/legacy/**/*.scss"]
rules = { "scss/max-nesting-depth" = "off" }
```

A scope's `remap` changes whole severities in its files, after everything else: `remap = { error = "warn" }` never fails the run there.

### Warn locally, fail in CI

The `ci` profile runs when `CI` is set; `local` otherwise; `--profile <name>` or `CODELAW_PROFILE` picks one.

```toml
[profile.local.rules]
"scss/max-nesting-depth" = "warn"

[profile.ci.rules]
"scss/max-nesting-depth" = "error"
```

### In `pyproject.toml` or `package.json`

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[tool.codelaw.rules]
"scss/max-nesting-depth" = { severity = "warn", options = { max = 6 } }
```

```json
{
  "codelaw": {
    "rules": {
      "scss/max-nesting-depth": {"severity": "warn", "options": {"max": 6}}
    }
  }
}
```

### Silence one finding

An inline `codelaw-ignore` always needs a reason; `expires=`, `warn_days=` and `by=` date it ([SR-LINTER](../../../records/0106_linter.md) decision 6).

- **SCSS:** `// codelaw-ignore scss/max-nesting-depth: <reason>`
- **Dated:** `// codelaw-ignore scss/max-nesting-depth expires=2026-12-31 by=you@example.com: <reason>`

### Keep today's findings, fail on new ones

```bash
codelaw baseline add --rule scss/max-nesting-depth --expires 2026-12-31 --reason "<why>"
```

See [SR-BASELINE](../../../records/0104_baseline-and-deprecations.md).

### See what applies

```bash
codelaw explain scss/max-nesting-depth       # what it wants, why, how to fix
codelaw check --rule scss/max-nesting-depth  # only this rule
codelaw config --print --for <file>          # the resolved setting, and where it came from
```

## How to fix

1. Lift the inner rule out and give it its own class.
2. Use `&-suffix` (BEM-style names) instead of a new level.

## Examples

### SCSS

#### Don't

```scss
.a {
  .b {
    .c {
      .d {
        .e {
          color: red;
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

#### Do

```scss
.a {
  .b {
    .c {
      .d {
        color: red;
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## Differences from the source

Nested properties (`font: { … }`) and at-rules such as `@media` and `@include` do not count as a level; only style rules do.
